newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Kuwaiti firm proposes $1 bln project for Zanzibar.
newsitem.headline: Kuwaiti firm proposes $1 bln project for Zanzibar.

text.p: Kuwaiti construction company MA Kharafi Group has proposed a $1 billion tourist and freeport resort on the Indian Ocean island of Zanzibar, a ministry of planning and investment official said on Wednesday.
The investment proposal follows a visit by senior company executives to the island from May 17 to May 24, said the official who declined to be identified by name.

"At the moment it's a proposal. They (Kharafi Group) came here for a feasibility study to see where they could make an investment. They will be coming back -- they've left an office here," the official told Reuters by telephone.

The privately-owned Guardian newspaper on Wednesday quoted a press statement from the state-run Zanzibar Investment Co (ZICO) as saying the resort would include a free port, airport, five-star hotel and golf course at a cost of $1 billion.

But nothing has been signed so far although the Kuwaiti company said it would be sending a team of engineers, architects, environmental specialists and economists to complete a plan of the project for submission to the isles government.
ZICO said MA Kharafi is a class A world contractor with a net worth of $16 billion and a gross annual turnover of $600 million. No details were available from Kharafi itself.
Semi-autonomous Zanzibar joined with mainland Tanganyika to form the United Republic of Tanzania in 1964.
